Fares and Pareto frontiers

Source: vignettes/articles/fares.Rmd
fares.Rmd

peabiru computes the fare of each public transport trip from a fare structure, which describes how much each ride costs and which transfers are discounted; the routing functions take it as fare_structure. With one, public transport is routed with the multi-criteria router (McRAPTOR), which keeps at each stop the trips that are faster or cheaper than the others, over time_window * draws_per_minute departure times sampled in the window.

The fare structure

setup_fare_structure() builds one where every route, fare type and transfer costs the same; edit it to follow the fare rules of the city.

fares <- setup_fare_structure(network, base_fare = 4.4, by = "MODE")
fares$fares_per_type
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   type   unlimited_transfers allow_same_route_transfer use_route_fare  fare
#>   <chr>  <lgl>               <lgl>                     <lgl>          <dbl>
#> 1 SUBWAY FALSE               FALSE                     FALSE            4.4
#> 2 BUS    FALSE               FALSE                     FALSE            4.4
#> 3 RAIL   FALSE               FALSE                     FALSE            4.4
head(fares$fares_per_transfer, 3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   first_leg second_leg  fare
#>   <chr>     <chr>      <dbl>
#> 1 BUS       SUBWAY       4.4
#> 2 SUBWAY    SUBWAY       4.4
#> 3 BUS       BUS          4.4

The rules: the first ride costs its route’s fare (the type’s fare, or the route’s own route_fare when the type has use_route_fare); a ride of the same type as the one before is free when the type has unlimited_transfers; otherwise, while fewer than max_discounted_transfers discounts were used, a ride boarded within transfer_time_allowance minutes of the previous boarding, with a row of fares_per_transfer for the two types (and not on the same route, unless the type has allow_same_route_transfer), brings the two rides to that row’s fare; any other ride costs its full fare. The total is capped at fare_cap.

fares$fares_per_transfer$fare <- 6.6   # two rides together
fares$transfer_time_allowance <- 60L   # within an hour

write_fare_structure() and read_fare_structure() write and read a structure as a .zip file of five CSV files (the settings and the three tables), to keep it or share it.

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".zip")
write_fare_structure(fares, path)
identical(read_fare_structure(path), fares)
#> [1] TRUE

Routing with fares

max_fare keeps, for each pair, the fastest trip that costs no more than it, in travel_time_matrix(), accessibility() and detailed_itineraries():

ttm <- travel_time_matrix(
  network, points, points,
  mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"), departure_datetime = departure,
  fare_structure = fares, max_fare = 4.4,
  draws_per_minute = 1, seed = 42
)
head(ttm)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   from_id         to_id           travel_time_p50
#>   <chr>           <chr>                     <int>
#> 1 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c00fffff               0
#> 2 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c007ffff               7
#> 3 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c077ffff              10
#> 4 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c03bffff               8
#> 5 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c033ffff              13
#> 6 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c0afffff              23

pareto_frontier() gives, for each pair, the travel time at each fare cutoff where it changes. monetary_cost is the cutoff as the router reads it, a 32-bit float.

pf <- pareto_frontier(
  network, points[1:3, ], points,
  mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"), departure_datetime = departure,
  fare_structure = fares, fare_cutoffs = c(0, 4.4, 6.6), seed = 42
)
head(pf)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   from_id         to_id           percentile travel_time monetary_cost
#>   <chr>           <chr>                <int>       <int>         <dbl>
#> 1 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c00fffff         50           0             0
#> 2 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c007ffff         50           7             0
#> 3 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c077ffff         50          10             0
#> 4 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c03bffff         50           8             0
#> 5 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c033ffff         50          13             0
#> 6 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c0afffff         50          23             0

In this sample, whose GTFS is frequency-based, the multi-criteria router finds no trip faster than walking (it does not ride lines given by frequency): with fares the travel times are the walking times. With scheduled feeds, such as those of Porto Alegre in the trip options article, the frontier lists the faster trips that cost more.

Alternative itineraries

detailed_itineraries(shortest_path = FALSE) lists the alternatives McRAPTOR finds, one per sequence of routes, up to suboptimal_minutes slower than the best; with a fare structure, each with its fare (total_fare) and the fare paid by the end of each leg (cumulative_fare). Networks whose GTFS has frequency-based trips cannot be used with public transport there, so this sample’s itineraries are by street:

trips <- detailed_itineraries(
  network, points[1:2, ], points[3:4, ], mode = "WALK",
  departure_datetime = departure, fare_structure = fares,
  drop_geometry = TRUE
)
trips[, c("from_id", "to_id", "option", "total_duration", "total_fare",
          "mode", "cumulative_fare")]
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   from_id         to_id   option total_duration total_fare mode  cumulative_fare
#>   <chr>           <chr>    <int>          <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>           <dbl>
#> 1 89a8100c00fffff 89a810…      1           10.9          0 WALK                0
#> 2 89a8100c007ffff 89a810…      1            9.5          0 WALK                0

Trip options

To see every trip worth considering between two points, faster or cheaper, with fewer transfers or less walking, and not only the fastest one, see trip_options(), peabiru’s own multi-criteria planner: Trip options.
